title: Who do you build with?
intro: Most of what goes wrong in a business is about people rather than product. This is the read on what you bring to a room, and what you cost it.
share_line: In a room I am the
og_line: Seven questions on what you bring to a room, and what you cost it.

cta.title: There are twelve of these
cta.label: Score all twelve
cta.blurb: This is one of twelve energies, seen through other people. The full Energy Discovery is 48 statements and scores all twelve.

questions.q: The best working relationship you have had was mostly:

options.a: Someone who noticed what I was not saying
Someone who got the whole group moving
Someone who left me alone to get on with it
Someone who was still there in year three

questions.q: A new person joins. Your first instinct:

options.a: Work out how they are actually doing
Get them into the room and talking
Give them something real and see what happens
Wait. I will know in a month
I read who has gone quiet and start there
I get it named so we can decide
I go and prove it instead of arguing
I ask what this looks like in a year

questions.q: What you want from the people around you:

options.a: To be told the truth early
To be pointed at something and left to it
To be asked the question nobody else asks
To still be here when it gets slow

questions.q: The kind of meeting you would cancel:

options.a: Any meeting that ends without a decision
The one where nobody says what they think
The one about next quarter, when the real question is next decade
The one that could have been the same as last time

questions.q: You are best to work with when:

options.a: Someone needs to feel understood
A group is stuck and needs a decision
Nobody has done it before
It has to still be running in five years

questions.q: You are hardest to work with when:

options.a: I carry other people's weather
I push a decision before people are ready
I disappear and build alone
I will not be hurried, even when speed matters

results.name: Dolphin
results.headline: You read the room before anyone says anything.
results.body: You know when a meeting has gone wrong before it shows. You adjust how you say things to who is hearing them.
results.cost: Carrying the room's weather and calling it your own.

results.name: Gorilla
results.headline: You get the group to something it can actually act on.
results.body: You notice who has not spoken. You take the part of the work nobody picked up, and you put the group's outcome above your position in it.

results.name: Cat
results.headline: You start before anyone tells you to.
results.body: You do not need the brief. You will have taught yourself most of what you needed by the time permission arrives.
results.cost: Solving alone what a conversation would have solved faster.

results.name: Panda
results.headline: You work at a rate you can still hold next year.
results.body: Your output is predictable, which makes you plannable. You finish long work without the scramble at the end.
results.cost: Missing a short window that needed an unsustainable push.

results.name: Unicorn
results.headline: You arrive at the answer nobody else considered.
results.body: You combine things that do not usually go together, and you question whether the standard way is right here rather than in general.
results.cost: Novelty chosen over the thing that would have worked.

results.name: Dragon
results.headline: You work towards something that will not pay off yet.
results.body: You connect today's task to why it is being done, and you can describe where this goes in a way other people can picture.
results.cost: A horizon so far out that this quarter never gets judged.
